summary: Added Indian, Chinese, Islamic and African intellectual traditions, with specific work-identity and authorship cautions. This batch shares a reference publisher; later batches must diversify evidence types.
next: Consult independent critical and reader material, and add modern, medieval and women philosophers.

sources.title: Nāgārjuna
sources.note: Emptiness and arguments against intrinsic nature shaped Buddhist philosophy across Asia; the entry distinguishes reliably attributed works from later name-attributions.
candidates: The Fundamental Wisdom of the Middle Way

targets.A: Adds Buddhist argumentative works and reception beyond European canons.
targets.B: Identifies Middle Way texts and distinguishes shorter treatises.
targets.P: Documents Nagarjuna's influence while qualifying uncertain biography.

sources.limits: Dates and attributions are uncertain; verse treatises need complete-work eligibility review.

sources.title: Śaṅkara
sources.note: Shankara systematized Advaita through consciousness, metaphysics and teaching methods. His extant commentaries concern the Brahmasutras, Gita and principal Upanishads.

targets.A: Adds Indian commentarial scholarship to book discovery.
targets.N: Identifies argumentative commentaries; exact English volumes remain unresolved.
targets.B: Treats commentaries as substantive philosophy, distinct from their root texts.
targets.P: Supports Shankara as systematizer rather than originator of the entire tradition.

sources.limits: Hagiographies are not dependable biography; root texts and commentaries must not be conflated.

sources.title: Ibn Sina [Avicenna]
sources.note: Avicenna integrated science and philosophy; the medical Canon influenced European teaching, while philosophical reception included revision and refutation across religious communities.

targets.A: Adds medicine and cross-cultural intellectual transmission.
targets.N: Supplies historical medical nonfiction, not current clinical authority.
targets.B: Shows Arabic philosophical reception and a link to Maimonides's Guide.
targets.P: Documents Avicenna's systematic contribution and contested reception.

sources.limits: One author's strong comparative influence judgment is not a global score.

sources.title: al-Farabi
sources.note: The Great Book of Music combines musical theory and philosophy. The entry flags missing complete English translations and describes medieval reception of Enumeration of the Sciences.

targets.A: Adds music and classification of knowledge; translation eligibility remains open.
targets.B: Documents philosophical works outside standard ethics/metaphysics lists.
targets.P: Supports al-Farabi's work in logic, philosophy and music.

sources.limits: Do not recommend an English edition before verifying it; biography and ethnic attribution are disputed.

sources.title: Mencius
sources.note: Mengzi's ethical cultivation and account of human nature invite comparison with Aristotle and Hume. The text was compiled by followers and later edited by Zhao Qi.

targets.A: Adds a Chinese ethical-political classic with transmission evidence.
targets.N: Identifies a recorded-dialogue philosophical collection, pending form review.
targets.B: Maps the received Mengzi text to virtue and human-nature debates.
targets.P: Supports Mencius's distinctive position and later reception.

sources.limits: Do not attribute the entire received compilation directly to one author's manuscript.

sources.title: Xunzi
sources.note: Xunzi's reputation shifted from frequent disapproval to renewed recognition. The received collection derives from posthumous editorial work; it is predominantly authentic but textually layered.

targets.A: Adds an early Chinese essay collection and changing-canon evidence.
targets.N: Adds collected ethical-political argument; distinguish essays from collected book.
targets.B: Offers a contrast with Mencius on human nature and cultivation.
targets.P: Shows that historical marginalization differs from philosophical significance.

sources.limits: Life dates are uncertain; source biography can distort philosophers' lives.

sources.title: Laozi
sources.note: Daodejing's ethical, political and spiritual interpretations differ. The text's influence is broad, but the existence of its traditionally named author is disputed.

targets.A: Adds an influential Chinese classic with author-identity uncertainty.
targets.B: Documents competing readings and text-author separation.
targets.P: Requires a disputed-historical-identity flag before person eligibility.

sources.limits: Do not infer an established historical individual from a surviving named text.

sources.title: African Sage Philosophy
sources.note: Oruka's Sage Philosophy records dialogues evidencing individual critical thought in African oral traditions, challenging the assumption that philosophy requires a written authorial corpus.
candidates: Sage Philosophy: Indigenous Thinkers and Modern Debate on African Philosophy

targets.A: Adds a documented African philosophical dialogue collection.
targets.B: Supplies a philosophical book and challenges text-only canon assumptions.
targets.P: Distinguishes named oral thinkers from undifferentiated communal beliefs.

sources.location: Introduction and examples from Oruka's project
sources.limits: Interview mediation and translation matter; oral thinkers need person-specific evidence.
